From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: ClearHealth MSA - security exhibit redlines & pen test language

Emma / Chloe —

Thanks for the package and the redlines. High-level legal feedback below (we can follow up on a call for any items you want to negotiate live):

1) Audit right scope & notice
- We prefer audit rights to be limited to SOC 2 (Type II) and documented security evidence; full access to production systems or raw logs is not acceptable. We can accept a vendor-produced redacted pen-test summary that excludes exploit code and PII.
- Notice period: our standard is 30 days for remote/desk audits and 45 days for onsite/interactive pen-testing conducted by third parties; we can be flexible but need 30 days minimum.

2) Mutuality
- Please accept reciprocal audit obligations only where absolutely necessary — we will not permit open-ended access to Redwood systems. Audit rights should be mutual and scoped to the account’s data and environment.

3) Data handling & redaction
- Any evidence shared must have PII redacted and be delivered under an NDA/secure portal. We will not share unredacted raw logs.

4) Compromise clause & remediation window
- Propose a 30-day remediation window for identified issues before any contractual remedies are triggered. We’d like to capture SLA/rollback triggers separately in the order form if needed.

5) Pen-test scheduling & evidentiary artifacts
- We accept pen-test summaries if they include: scope, tester name, high-level findings, and confirmation of remediation where applicable. Full reports may be available under a more restricted process (legal-to-legal request).

Requests from our side to help close quickly:
- Please confirm the external tester name and whether the pen-test includes infrastructure, application, or both.
- Share the SOC 2 auditor name and the date range covered by the attestation.
- Provide a DocuSign link to the redlines (or confirm you’ll accept our counter redlines back through DocuSign).

If these high-level positions are acceptable, we can prepare an internal redline (clean MSA + security exhibit comments) and push to you by EOD Thursday. If there are standouts we should negotiate, we should take them on a short call — Chloe, please confirm Thursday 10:00 PT or propose alternates.

— Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: ClearHealth MSA - security exhibit redlines & audit window coordination

Emma / team —

Thanks for the details and attachments. From a security operations standpoint, Redwood’s acceptable evidence cadence and coordination preferences are below: 

- Evidence accepted: SOC 2 Type II report (PDF) + vendor pen-test executive summary (redacted). We will not accept raw logs or exploit code via standard redaction rules.
- Access method: secure transfer via vendor portal or our secure SFTP; for particularly sensitive artifacts we’ll use a signed NDA + secure link.
- Audit cadence: annual SOC2 attestation is sufficient for most customers. For additional assurance, a rolling 12-month pen-test summary (latest within 12 months) is acceptable.
- Pen-test windows: if ClearHealth wants Redwood to participate in an interactive pen-test, please propose preferred windows; Redwood operations needs 30–45 days lead time depending on scope.
- Evidence retention & request window: Redwood requests up to 30 days to review evidence after submission; if remediation verification is needed, allow an additional 30 days to validate fixes.

Suggested contract language (high-level):
"Customer may request evidence of Redwood’s security posture in the form of a SOC 2 Type II report and a redacted third-party penetration test executive summary. Requests for live, interactive testing involving Redwood infrastructure require at least 30 days' prior written notice; Redwood reserves the right to require up to 45 days' notice for high-impact tests and to coordinate scheduling to prevent service disruption."

If that language is acceptable to ClearHealth, Laura and I can work with Chloe to convert into a short security exhibit counter-redline and push via DocuSign.

-Aditya
Security Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
